fields.meta_title: DJ Landing Page Builder for Gigs and Bookings | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a DJ landing page from one prompt. See four examples: wedding gig requests, a capped club night list, a gated mix, and a press kit.
fields.h1: Build a DJ Landing Page That Books Your Next Gig
fields.hero_description: Build a DJ landing page that takes gig requests, caps RSVPs at the room limit, and saves every fan to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Behind the Decks
fields.features_subheading: A DJ landing page has one job: turn a listener into a booking or a fan. Emergent builds the page and the records behind it.
fields.feature_1:
Requests that carry the gig details

Emergent builds the request form a booking needs: event date, venue, start and end time, and guest count. Every inquiry is stored as one row you can sort by date or by venue.
fields.feature_2:
An alert when a new date comes in

The app sends you an email or a Slack alert when a request arrives, with the event date and venue in the message. You can reply to the planner before another DJ takes the date.
fields.feature_3:
Your mixes playing on the page

Paste a SoundCloud link and Emergent places the player in your page. SoundCloud's oEmbed endpoint serves the widget embed code for a SoundCloud URL that points to a playlist.
fields.feature_4:
A fan list that stays yours

Each email a fan enters is saved to a database you own, along with the page and date it came from. Connect that list to your email tool over its API when the next mix goes out.
fields.feature_5:
Your own domain, edited by prompt

Publish on your own domain (custom domains are included and use credits). If the residency moves to Thursdays, tell Emergent in one prompt and it changes the date on the page.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

The free tier covers building and publishing your page. On paid plans, Emergent exports the full code to your GitHub repository, ready for a developer to pick up later.

fields.tab_content_1:
Every inquiry lands with its date

Vega Sound Co. plays weddings, and its request page asks each couple for the date, the venue, the set length, and the guest count before anything else. The app saves every inquiry as one row and emails it to the owner, Mateo Vega. The Larkspur Barn request for June 12 asked for a 5-hour set and 140 guests.
fields.tab_content_2:
An RSVP list with a hard cap

Basement Frequencies throws one club night a month in a room that holds 180 people. Its page takes free RSVPs, counts each one against the cap, and closes the list at 180, when a waitlist signup replaces the form. The October night filled all 180 spots, and 37 more people joined the waitlist.
fields.tab_content_3:
Email in before the mix plays

Noa Lindqvist released Solstice Mix Vol. 7 on a page where the player starts once a listener enters an email. The app saves each address to her fan list with the name of the mix it unlocked. In its first week the mix brought in 318 new emails, and she exports the list before every release.
fields.tab_content_4:
The one page a booker reads

Arlo Finch sends talent buyers one link with his bio, the 4 rooms he played this year, and a stage plot. A booking button opens a short avails form that asks for the venue, the date, and its capacity. Each request is saved for Arlo to answer, and the Halden Hall request for March 6 came in at 900 capacity.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a DJ Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps take a DJ landing page from one booking goal to a tested page that saves every request and fan email.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the gig you want more of
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Lead with a mix they can hear
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for what you need to quote
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Show proof a booker can check
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide which job the page has to win, such as wedding inquiries or fans for your mixes. A couple planning a reception and a talent buyer filling a lineup look for different things on a page. Build for one of them first, and add the other later.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put one recent mix near the top, matched to the gig: a wedding set for couples, a peak-time recording for promoters. Thirty seconds of your blends tells a visitor more than a paragraph listing the genres you play.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write down what you need before you can price a date: the day, the room, the hours you will play, and how many people are coming. Put only those questions in the request form and save the rest for the first call.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Name the rooms and residencies you have played, with dates where you have them. Add a short bio in plain words and a stage plot or rider that a promoter can forward to the production manager at the venue.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set the rule for a full night
fields.howto_step_5_des: If the page takes RSVPs for your own night, set the cap at the number the venue gives you or lower. Then decide what visitors see once it fills, such as a waitlist signup or the date of the next night.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose who hears about a new inquiry and how: an email to you, a Slack message to your agent, or both. Keep every request in one table, where a double-booked Saturday shows up before you say yes to it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it with a fake booking
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit a request from your phone with a real date and venue, then check the saved row and the alert that reaches you. Describe the page to Emergent and change any part by prompt until the test reads right.

faq_plan.q: What is a dj landing page?
faq_plan.a: A DJ landing page is a single web page built to get one action from a visitor: a booking request, an RSVP for a night, or an email signup for a new mix. It leads with a sample of your sound and puts the form for that one action right under it.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a dj landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the page in a prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder: the gigs you play, the mix to feature, and what a booking request should collect. From that prompt Emergent writes the page, its form, and a database for every request. You change any part later by asking for it.

faq_plan.q: What should a DJ landing page include?
faq_plan.a: Include one recent mix, a short bio, the venues or events you have played, and a booking form. Promoters also look for a stage plot or rider they can pass on. Keep a single action at the top of the page and move everything else below it.

faq_plan.q: Can a DJ landing page promote a weekly radio show or mix series?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each episode its own entry with the player and its tracklist, and put an email signup for the next episode under it. If the show is mostly talk with little music, a podcast landing page fits it better.

faq_plan.q: Is a DJ landing page enough, or do I need a full website?
faq_plan.a: A DJ landing page is enough when you want one result, such as wedding bookings or signups for a mix series. Move to a full site once you need several sections at once, such as a mix archive and separate pages for each type of event.

faq_plan.q: How do I avoid double bookings with a DJ landing page?
faq_plan.a: Check each new request against one list of confirmed dates before you say yes. You can ask Emergent to build that check into the form: once you accept a gig, the app marks the date as held, and a second request for the same Saturday appears as a conflict.

faq_plan.q: How can a DJ landing page grow a fan email list?
faq_plan.a: Trade the email for something fans want: an unreleased edit, a full set recording, or early ticket access. Put the signup beside the player and ask for an email and a city only. If your audience comes mostly from social video and brand work, an influencer landing page is the closer fit.

faq_plan.q: How do I get more gigs from a DJ landing page?
faq_plan.a: Send people to it from every place a booker finds you, such as your social bios and the QR code on your business card. Then compare which source sends the most requests. When Emergent builds the page, every request lands in a database you own, tagged with the link that sent it.

faq_plan.q: Should a DJ landing page use a domain with my DJ name?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you can. A domain with your DJ name looks more established on a rider or a business card, and it is easier to say out loud at a gig. Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits.

faq_plan.q: Can a DJ landing page take sign-ups for lessons?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a lessons section with the format, the length of each session, and a request form that asks about the student's experience and gear. If you plan a full program with weekly modules and lessons to watch, a course landing page suits it better.
